description:
Tests in tests/unit/platforms/credentials/test_bigquery_defaults.py (class TestBigQueryCredentialDefaults) fail intermittently in the `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)` CI job (ci.yml:721, job id code-test) and pass when the file, or the whole tests/unit/scripts and credentials scope, runs locally. On a pull request the failure fails the required `core` unit and blocks auto-merge until the job is rerun. On develop it fails trunk.yml fast.

Observed failures, all in the full-suite xdist run (worker gw0), on unrelated code changes:
- test_skips_auto_detection_when_credentials_exist: `assert mock_confirm.call_count == 1` -> `AssertionError: assert 0 == 1` (CI run 36865382651).
- test_works_with_no_existing_credentials: `calls[2][1]["current_value"]` at test_bigquery_defaults.py:134 -> `IndexError: list index out of range`, so fewer prompt calls were recorded than the setup flow makes (CI run 36910191689, job 110531036486).
- Still flaking on 2026-10-09: CI run 37957451111, job 113914156328.

The likely failure mode: another test file on the same xdist worker replaces the global `rich.prompt.Confirm`, so the test patches a stale object while production code calls the real prompt. The tests already patch `benchbox.platforms.credentials.bigquery.Confirm.ask` rather than `rich.prompt.Confirm.ask`, and the flake persists, so the root cause is not removed. The class comment that once described this was removed in #2614.

Leads:
- Sibling credential tests still patch `rich.prompt.Confirm.ask` globally (test_databricks_defaults.py, test_redshift_defaults.py, and others); check whether they or any other test rebinds or reloads `rich.prompt` or `benchbox.platforms.credentials.bigquery` without restoring it.
- Look for module reloads, `sys.modules` edits, or `importlib.reload` in the unit suite that leave `benchbox.platforms.credentials.bigquery.Confirm` bound to a different object than the one the tests patch.
- Reproduce with a pinned xdist ordering (`-p xdist -n 2 --dist loadfile` or the CI worker count and seed) and bisect which co-scheduled test file causes it.
- tests/utilities/leak_detector.py already snapshots registered globals between tests (REGISTERED_GLOBALS, line 10); it is the natural place for a guard.
